# `builtin:fault`

Installs a Linux netem qdisc on a target container's network interface -
delay, jitter, packet loss, corruption, duplication, and reordering, all
composed into one qdisc - via the relay's privileged netlink access.
Operates purely at the network-namespace level: no interaction with
[`builtin:route`]({{< relref "/docs/reference/steps/route" >}}) or the kevin
proxy at all.

A fault step never names a target by path - only by `needs`. With no
`containers` set, it faults every container every needs entry resolves to,
which is enough for the common case (a
[`builtin:container`]({{< relref "/docs/reference/steps/container" >}})
step reports exactly one, so there's nothing to narrow):

```cue
backend: {uses: "builtin:container", with: {image: "myapp/backend"}}

backend_fault: {
    uses:  "builtin:fault"
    needs: ["backend"]
    with: {
        delay_ms:     200
        loss_percent: 10
    }
}
```

A [`builtin:kind`]({{< relref "/docs/reference/steps/kind" >}}) cluster
reports one container per node - name a `workers` key
(see that reference page) to fault it individually, or two of them
at once:

```cue
cluster: {uses: "builtin:kind", with: {workers: {worker_a: {}, worker_b: {}}}}

worker_fault: {
    uses:  "builtin:fault"
    needs: ["cluster"]
    with: {
        containers:   ["worker_a", "worker_b"]
        loss_percent: 25
    }
}
```

`containers` matches the literal name you already declared - `worker_a`
in `cluster`'s own `workers` map, or (for a single-container step like
`backend` above) that step's own name as a fallback: `containers:
["backend"]` works too, even though `builtin:container` itself reports
`"kevin-demo-backend"`. Cross-scope works the same way `needs` already
does: `needs: ["setup.registry"]`, and `"registry"` still resolves as
that step's fallback name.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|:------|:----:|:-------:|:------------|
| `containers` | `[...string]` | - | Narrows which container this fault impairs, by name. Unset means every container every needs entry resolves to - a builtin:kind cluster with no other needs entries, say, faults every node identically. A name matches either a container's own name (as reported by its step - see the reference doc for how each plugin determines it), or, when a needs step manages exactly one container, that step's own name as a fallback: `"cache"` works whether the step reporting it is a builtin:container step or the one worker of a builtin:kind cluster. |
| `interface` | `string` | - | The network interface inside the target container to impair. Empty picks the relay's own default (`"eth0"`). |
| `delay_ms` | `int & >0` | - | The fixed one-way delay added to every packet, in milliseconds. |
| `jitter_ms` | `int & >=0` | - | The random variation applied around delay_ms, in milliseconds. Only meaningful alongside delay_ms. |
| `loss_percent` | `float & >0 & <=100` | - | The percentage of packets dropped. |
| `corrupt_percent` | `float & >0 & <=100` | - | The percentage of packets corrupted (a single bit flipped). |
| `duplicate_percent` | `float & >0 & <=100` | - | The percentage of packets duplicated. |
| `reorder_percent` | `float & >0 & <=100` | - | The percentage of packets reordered ahead of delay_ms. Only meaningful alongside delay_ms. |

At least one impairment field must be set; `Up` rejects an otherwise-empty
`with` block. A `containers` entry naming nothing any needs step reports
is an `Up`-time error - as is an empty `with` block when no needs step
reports any container at all.

**Kind: action.** A fault step deploys nothing itself: it tells the relay
how to treat a namespace another step already created. It has no `Down` -
the engine clears every fault it applied at teardown on its own,
independent of whether a step's plugin implements `Down` at all.

Idempotent: re-`Up`-ing with a changed config replaces each netem qdisc's
parameters, matching how Linux's own `tc qdisc replace` behaves.
